F-36 ALIS Compliance Bridge Assessment — Fort Worth Plant

The following SPARTA countermeasures have been mapped against NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls and DISA STIG checks for the F-36 Autonomic Logistics Information System (ALIS).

ST-1 Denial of Service Protection: The F-36 ALIS ground segment requires protection against denial-of-service attacks targeting maintenance scheduling systems. Maps to NIST SC-5 (Denial-of-Service Protection), SC-7 (Boundary Protection), and CP-9 (System Backup). DISA STIG checks V-219151 (network DoS protection) and V-219152 (application layer DoS filtering) verify implementation. Full bidirectional traceability established. Coverage: 85%.

ST-2 Link Encryption: All ALIS data transfers between Fort Worth plant terminals and the central mission data server must use FIPS 140-2 validated encryption. Maps to NIST SC-8 (Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity), SC-12 (Cryptographic Key Establishment), SC-13 (Cryptographic Protection). DISA STIG checks V-219160 (TLS configuration) and V-219161 (certificate validation). Bidirectional. Coverage: 92%.

ST-3 Authentication Spoofing Prevention: ALIS terminal authentication must prevent credential replay and spoofing attacks. Maps to NIST SC-8, IA-2 (Identification and Authentication), IA-5 (Authenticator Management). Single STIG check V-219170 (MFA enforcement) — additional STIG coverage needed for smart card authentication. Bidirectional but incomplete. Coverage: 78%.

ST-4 Replay Attack Mitigation: Session replay attacks against ALIS maintenance workflows must be mitigated via nonce-based challenge-response. Maps to NIST SC-8 and SC-23 (Session Authenticity). No DISA STIG checks currently mapped — GAP IDENTIFIED. Forward mapping only. Coverage: 45%.

ST-5 Malicious Code Prevention: F-36 OFP build pipeline and ALIS software distribution must prevent malicious code insertion. Maps to NIST SI-3 (Malicious Code Protection), SI-7 (Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity), CM-3 (Configuration Change Control). Three STIG checks: V-219180 (AV scanning), V-219181 (integrity verification), V-219182 (change control audit). Full bidirectional. Coverage: 95%.

ST-6 Ground Station Hardening: ALIS ground terminals at Fort Worth maintenance bays require physical and logical access controls. Maps to NIST AC-17 (Remote Access), SC-7 (Boundary Protection), PE-3 (Physical Access Control). STIG V-219190 (terminal lockdown policy). Bidirectional. Coverage: 88%.

ST-7 Supply Chain Integrity: F-36 vendor-supplied avionics components and FADEC firmware must maintain integrity throughout the supply chain. Maps to NIST SA-12 (Supply Chain Protection), SI-7, SR-3 (Supply Chain Controls and Processes). No DISA STIG checks currently mapped — CRITICAL GAP. The F135 FADEC vendor supply chain has no STIG verification. Forward only. Coverage: 35%.

ST-8 Insider Threat Monitoring: ALIS user activity monitoring for privileged maintenance personnel at Fort Worth. Maps to NIST AC-2 (Account Management), AC-6 (Least Privilege), AU-6 (Audit Record Review), PE-3. STIG checks V-219200 (privileged access monitoring) and V-219201 (audit log review procedures). Bidirectional. Coverage: 90%.

ST-9 RF Interference Protection: F-36 ground-to-air data links must be resilient against RF jamming during maintenance data uploads. Maps to NIST SC-5, CP-9 (System Backup for degraded RF conditions). No STIG checks — RF resilience not covered by current DISA STIGs for ground maintenance systems. Forward only. Coverage: 40%.

ST-10 Data Loss Prevention: ALIS must prevent unauthorized exfiltration of classified F-36 maintenance records and avionics diagnostic data. Maps to NIST SC-8, SC-13, MP-4 (Media Storage), AC-6. STIG checks V-219210 (DLP endpoint agent) and V-219211 (removable media controls). Bidirectional. Coverage: 82%.

F-36 ALIS NIST 800-171 Compliance Proof Structure — Fort Worth Plant

Top-level compliance goal: The F-36 ALIS system at the Fort Worth plant complies with NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 for protection of CUI in nonfederal systems.

Level 1 decomposition:
- L1.1 Access Control (AC): All ALIS terminals enforce role-based access per 800-171 3.1.x. Status: PROVEN. Evidence: annual assessment report dated 2026-01. Importance: 0.95. Controls: AC-2, AC-6, AC-17.
- L1.2 Audit and Accountability (AU): ALIS audit logging captures all maintenance actions with tamper-evident storage. Status: PROVEN. Evidence: SIEM integration verified. Importance: 0.85. Controls: AU-2, AU-6, AU-12.
- L1.3 System and Communications Protection (SC): All ALIS network communications use FIPS-validated encryption with boundary protection. Status: UNPROVEN. Evidence gap: SC-7 boundary assessment incomplete for new plant expansion wing. Importance: 0.90. Failure probability: 0.35. Controls: SC-7, SC-8, SC-13.

Level 2 decomposition:
- L2.1 Remote Access Control (under L1.1): VPN access to ALIS from remote depot sites uses MFA. Status: PROVEN. Evidence: Duo MFA logs. Importance: 0.80. Controls: AC-17.
- L2.2 Audit Log Integrity (under L1.2): Centralized SIEM with write-once storage for ALIS audit trails. Status: PROVEN. Importance: 0.75. Controls: AU-9.
- L2.3 Boundary Protection (under L1.3): ALIS VLAN segmentation from corporate network. Status: UNPROVEN. The new Building 7 maintenance expansion connects to ALIS VLAN but firewall rules have not been updated. Importance: 0.90. Failure probability: 0.60. Controls: SC-7.
- L2.4 Encryption in Transit (under L1.3): TLS 1.3 for all ALIS data transfers. Status: PROVEN. Evidence: TLS certificate audit. Importance: 0.85. Controls: SC-8.

Level 3 decomposition:
- L3.1 Least Privilege (under L2.1): ALIS maintenance roles follow least privilege — no shared admin accounts. Status: PROVEN. Importance: 0.70. Controls: AC-6.
- L3.2 Building 7 Firewall Rules (under L2.3): Specific firewall ACLs for Building 7 ALIS terminals. Status: CONTRADICTED. Assessment found Building 7 terminals have unrestricted VLAN access due to temporary construction bypass that was never revoked. This contradicts L2.3 boundary protection claim. Importance: 0.95. Failure probability: 0.85. Controls: SC-7.

Dependency edges:
- L1.1 depends_on L2.1 (weight 0.8)
- L1.2 depends_on L2.2 (weight 0.9)
- L1.3 depends_on L2.3 (weight 0.95) — critical: if boundary fails, SC compliance fails
- L1.3 depends_on L2.4 (weight 0.7)
- L2.1 depends_on L3.1 (weight 0.6)
- L2.3 depends_on L3.2 (weight 1.0) — hard dependency
- L3.2 contradicts L2.3 (weight 0.9) — Building 7 bypass contradicts boundary protection claim
- L1.1 generalizes L1.2 (weight 0.3) — access control subsumes audit accountability at high level
